alternatives.transcript: An agency phone is a dialing or messaging number that we own. There is only one record right now, and at first glance that does not look like a very important object. It is actually one of the most consequential in the whole library, Because that single row is the thing that decides whether every call we place and every text we send is allowed to happen at all. Get it wrong, and the carrier or the regulator takes the number away, and suddenly the entire outbound engine, the calls and the messages and the leads and the conversations, all of it stops. The fields are mostly regulatory housekeeping, and that is the point. There is the phone number itself, and the country code, so the system knows which country's rules apply. There is the number type, so it is clear whether this is a local number, a mobile, or a toll free line. Then the state field, which is simply the current status of the number. And then the three registration identifiers, which are the real payload. There is a 10 DLC campaign ID, which is The United States registration for business texting. There is a toll free verification ID, which is the separate check toll free numbers have to pass before they can send. And there is a messaging profile ID, which is the Telmix profile. The number sends through. Why is compliance stored in the CRM at all, rather than just in somebody's head? Because compliance is not a preference. It is a hard constraint imposed by carriers and regulators who are not interested in our pipeline. If a number is not registered properly, text messages to it get silently dropped. If complaint rates go too high on a campaign, the messaging profile is suspended. If we try to send from a number that has not passed toll free verification, nothing arrives and no error is shown. So this object is our single source of truth for whether our outbound is actually permitted. One row enormous blast radius: Where does it get used in practice? At the moment of sending, before anything goes out, the messaging system reads this record, checks the profile is active, checks the registration is valid, and only then releases the message. That is the whole point of putting it in the database it turns a legal constraint into an automated precondition. When something is not working and texts are mysteriously not landing, this is the first record you open. And if you ever want to add a second number, a new city, or a different channel, you duplicate this row, get it registered properly first, and only then start sending. Never the other way round.
